title: arvo-extension.json
description: What an Arvo extension declares about itself. Everything under `contributes` is optional; an extension may contribute several kinds at once.

id.description: The extension's own name, and the folder it installs into. Namespaces everything it contributes, so two packs may both ship a theme called `midnight`.

name.description: What to call it in a list. Falls back to the id.

version.description: The extension's own version, shown in the Extensions view.

webviews.description: Declared so an extension that ships one is recognised and refused rather than silently installed as if it were data. No third-party code runs in Arvo's window.

base.description: The built-in palette this one starts from, so a theme that names six colours still has the other forty.

colors.description: CSS custom properties by their own names. A property Arvo does not know, or a value that is not a colour, is dropped.

interval.description: A bar's resolution: a count of some unit.

strategy.description: A strategy as data: a kind, and that kind's parameters.

name.description: Namespaced by the extension in the picker: `their-catalog.fast-cross`.

premise.description: One line on what it trades. A name is not a description.

grid.description: A rule Arvo implements, searched over parameters you choose. It cannot contribute a rule.

rule.description: The rule Arvo knows by this name. One it does not have is refused when the manifest is read, with the list of what it does have.

fixed.description: Parameters every trial shares. The rule's own are inherited; these override the ones named.

axes.description: What the search varies, and over what values. An axis with no values searches nothing and is refused.

rules.description: Thresholds over named signals. Arvo reads one; it has no runner for one yet.

ruleSet.description: An empty set never holds, in either direction: all-of over nothing is vacuously true in logic and would mean `enter on every bar` here.

rule.description: One threshold over one named signal. Both bounds absent asks only whether the signal is known. A rule over an absent value is false.

provider.description: A process Arvo starts, speaking gRPC over loopback. See PROTOCOL.md.

services.description: The gRPC services it serves. `arvo.source.v1.Source` is the one that exists.

build.description: How to build it, as argv split on whitespace. No shell runs it.

run.description: What to run: a path to the file the build produced, or a command to run in the checkout.

assets.description: Prebuilt binaries, one per platform, for a machine with no toolchain. When every provider offers one for the running platform, Arvo downloads instead of building.

target.description: The target triple it was built for: `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.

sha256.description: Checked before the file is written. This is an executable Arvo will run with the person's privileges.
